To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of green tea as a reducing agent in the synthesis of silver nanoparticles supported on carbonaceous material (from sewage sludge) is a promising alternative to remove methylene blue dye in aqueous solutions, with high efficiency, without using sunlight or ultraviolet radiation.

a new nanocomposite, based on silver nanoparticles supported on carbonaceous material, was successfully prepared and applied as a heterogeneous photocatalyst to the removal of methylene blue from aqueous solution.

the use of a carbonaceous material from the pyrolysate of sewage sludge, in combination with green tea aqueous extract, as reducing agent, allows the synthesis of Ag NPs, which were successfully immobilized on the carbonaceous support, and the obtained composite showed high catalytic activity for the removal of MB in aqueous solution.

the synthesis of Ag-CM composite, and its use as a catalyst for the removal of organic dyes from wastewater.
the development of a new material with high potential in the treatment of water and wastewater, and the results obtained are very promising.
the development of an eco-friendly, simple and low-cost methodology to synthesize Ag-CM nanocomposite and its use as a promising catalyst for MB removal from aqueous solution.
